review: The source differs from the prior reviewed concurrent-session module only in bound_release: it now checks stop_machine's result when disarming a running session. On success it dismisses the session as before. On failure the session is still armed, so a probe handler may still reach it through watch[slot]; release then leaves it allocated, keeps its MM reference and its admitted slot, and logs one warning, so no armed session is ever freed and no slot is reused while a probe can read it. The leak is bounded by the 32 slots; a later open finds the slot taken.

Everything else is as in the prior review, which this one carries forward: up to 32 sessions of distinct MMs, admit() refusing a second session for an MM and a 33rd session with -EBUSY (the open fails, so the run fails rather than undercounting), count_positive() crediting each counter update to the one armed session that owns the counter and invalidating it on a foreign update or overflow, watch[slot] written only inside stop_machine, the global missed-probe and control-file checks voiding every session they overlap, and the unchanged bound of initial summed RSS plus every positive counter update until END.
check.c and prove.sh are unchanged in behaviour apart from prove.sh waiting on each of the four concurrent held checks by its process id, so any failing check fails the proof.
